scope: GSPA founding-governance actors: political/senior-state-actor threshold verification

findings.claim: The first GSPA dean was not merely an academic actor. The Academy of Korean Studies records his later service as Minister of Reconstruction in 1961 and first Minister of National Unification, in addition to SNU presidency and economic-policy advisory roles.
findings.caution: The encyclopedia verifies ministerial offices but does not by itself establish his personal authorship of the 1959 GSPA decree, admissions policy, or curriculum. Those remain separate claims.

findings.claim: The acting GSPA dean in 1960-1961 also crossed the cabinet threshold: the Academy of Korean Studies records his appointment as Minister of Education when the post-April Revolution transitional cabinet was formed in 1960, and earlier four-year service as chair of the Ministry of National Defense war-history compilation committee during/after the Korean War.
findings.caution: His ministerial tenure overlaps the transition into his acting GSPA deanship only at the boundary; exact appointment orders must be used before asserting day-level overlap or causal responsibility.

findings.claim: A Korea Democracy Foundation chronology records that on 1960-06-23 Education Minister Lee Byeong-do publicly argued that the teachers union should be dissolved, while union representatives countered that organization was lawful and issued a resignation recommendation.
findings.caution: The chronology cites contemporary Chosun Ilbo and Dong-A Ilbo reports; those newspaper pages and ministry directives should be recovered before modeling the exact legal/administrative action.

findings.claim: The Academy of Korean Studies identifies Shin as a professor at SNU Law College, later SNU president, 1961 Reconstruction Minister, Bank of Korea monetary-policy committee member, and first National Unification Minister. This establishes a durable academic-state-policy bridge suitable for an independent annals node.

adversarial_checks: Do not infer that Shin Tae-hwan authored the January 1959 Presidential Decree solely because he was first dean.
Do not infer that Lee Byeong-do shaped GSPA founding policy solely because he later served as acting dean.
Do not merge Lee Byeong-do's cabinet office, academic office, and Defense Ministry historical-compilation role into one undifferentiated political role.
Do not treat later biographical encyclopedias as substitutes for appointment orders when exact dates and legal authority are material.
Do not infer direct presidential instruction for either actor's later cabinet conduct without cabinet/presidential records.
Do not treat the Korea Democracy Foundation chronology as the underlying ministerial directive; recover the directive and contemporary press it cites.
Do not classify the teachers-union dispute as a GSPA event merely because Lee also served in GSPA governance; link through the person node, not institutional conflation.
Do not infer that all economic-policy advisory positions held by Shin carried executive decision authority.
Do not silently resolve variant Romanizations; retain aliases for retrieval.
Do not extend the verified ministerial threshold finding to the other GSPA deans without independent career evidence.
